name: gpredict
why: Real-time satellite orbit prediction you can run at home, and it pairs with radios to track passes overhead.

brief.what_it_is: Gpredict is a free, GPL-licensed real-time satellite tracking and orbit prediction application. It tracks a large number of satellites and shows their position and other data in lists, tables, maps, and polar plots (radar view). It can also predict the times of a satellite's future passes and give detailed information about each pass. You can track satellites relative to several observer locations at the same time.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage positions Gpredict as different from other satellite tracking programs because you can group satellites into visualisation modules, each configured independently, so you can control the look and feel of each module.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the orbit-prediction mechanism. It describes the user-facing model: satellites are grouped into modules, each module has its own configuration, and each module can track satellites relative to a chosen observer location.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says Gpredict is available as a source package and as precompiled binaries from third parties. It does not give build dependencies, first-run steps, or any hardware, account, or configuration requirements. The brew formula is the only install route I can confirm from the registry info, and I did not check the Download page.
brief.standout: Satellite groups are placed into separate visualisation modules that can each be configured on their own, and one instance can track passes for several observer locations at once. The homepage presents this as the main difference from other tracking programs.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage footer says 'Updated: Thursday, 18 Jun 2026, 13:18 UTC by Alexandru Csete', which is the page's last edit date, not a software release date. I did not find a release or commit date, and I did not reach the project's download or changelog pages.
brief.caveats: The homepage is marketing-style and gives no commands, install steps, or supported-platform list. The scout note says it 'pairs with radios to track passes overhead', but the homepage text I read does not mention radio control or pairing, so that claim is unverified here. The Features, Screenshots, Download, Documents, and Roadmap sections were listed but their link targets were not returned, so I could not follow them.

entry.title: gpredict
entry.tldr: A desktop app that tracks satellites in real time, draws their orbits on maps and radar plots, and predicts when they will pass over you.
entry.deeper_look:
Gpredict is a free, GPL-licensed satellite tracking and orbit prediction application. It follows a large number of satellites and shows their positions and other data in lists, tables, maps, and polar plots, the radar-style view of where something is in your sky. It can also predict future passes and give detailed information about each one.

The idea that sets it apart, according to its homepage, is the module. You group satellites into visualisation modules, and each module is configured on its own, so you control the look and feel of each. A single instance can also track satellites relative to several observer locations at once, so you can compare what is overhead at home with what is overhead somewhere else.

Underneath is a question worth chewing on: how do you know where a thing in orbit is, right now, from a spot on the ground? The homepage does not explain the prediction mechanism, so that part is yours to dig into. It is a good door into orbital mechanics, and into the amateur radio world where people listen for passes.

The project's own words: "Gpredict is a real-time satellite tracking and orbit prediction application." It installs hamlib as a dependency, which hints at radio-related use, but the homepage text does not say what that covers.
entry.install:
brew install gpredict
# GTK desktop app: needs a graphical session, no account or hardware required to start

try_this.what_happens: Opens the GUI, where you can set up a module, pick an observer location, and watch satellites on the map and polar plot.
Lists the command-line options the program accepts.

entry.whats_unique: Satellites are grouped into independently configured modules, and one instance can track passes for several observer locations at once.
entry.caveats: It is a GUI app, and the homepage I read gave no install steps, platform list, or release date, so how actively it is maintained is unconfirmed.
